ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.note: Spoon flour into the cup and level it — scooping straight from the bag packs in up to 25% more flour, the #1 cause of dense baked goods.

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.note: Granulated sugar pours consistently, so cup measurements are reliable — but weight is still faster for scaling recipes.

ingredients.name: Brown Sugar (packed)
ingredients.note: Brown sugar is always measured packed — pressed firmly into the cup until it holds its shape when turned out.

ingredients.name: Powdered Sugar
ingredients.note: Powdered sugar compacts in the bag; sift or whisk it before measuring by volume, or just weigh it.

ingredients.name: Butter
ingredients.note: In the US, butter math is easiest in sticks: 1 stick = ½ cup = 8 tablespoons = 113 grams.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.note: Honey is heavy — 1.4× the weight of the same volume of water. Grease the measuring cup and it slides right out.

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.note: Liquids are the one case where volume is as accurate as weight — a cup of milk is 240 g almost exactly.

ingredients.name: Rice (uncooked)
ingredients.note: A cup of dry white rice (185 g) cooks up to about 3 cups — plan a quarter to a third of a cup dry per side-dish serving.

ingredients.name: Rolled Oats
ingredients.note: Rolled oats are light — a cup is only about 90 g. Steel-cut oats are denser at about 160 g per cup.

ingredients.name: Cocoa Powder
ingredients.note: Cocoa clumps and compacts like flour — spoon and level it, or weigh it, especially in chocolate cakes where it replaces flour.

ingredients.name: Peanut Butter
ingredients.note: Sticky and dense — 270 g per cup. A greased or wet measuring cup releases it cleanly.

ingredients.name: Cornstarch
ingredients.note: One tablespoon of cornstarch (7.5 g) thickens about one cup of liquid to sauce consistency.
